vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Quality control plots}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

ProteoVaultR plots precursor and protein-group quantity distributions from the core DIA-NN matrices. The plots exclude missing and nonpositive quantities and use a log2 scale.

```{r}
library(ProteoVaultR)

fixture <- file.path("..", "tests", "fixtures", "example-vault.duckdb")
vault <- open_vault(path = fixture)

precursor_plot <- plot_precursor_quantity_distribution(
    vault = vault,
    quantity_type = "normalized",
    plot_type = "boxplot"
)
protein_plot <- plot_protein_quantity_distribution(
    vault = vault,
    plot_type = "violin"
)

precursor_plot
protein_plot
```

Raw precursor quantities and a `max_q_value` filter use the DIA-NN report imported during the core build. The cutoff only filters rows present in the report; it cannot restore rows DIA-NN omitted.

```{r}
raw_plot <- plot_precursor_quantity_distribution(
    vault = vault,
    quantity_type = "raw",
    plot_type = "boxplot",
    max_q_value = 0.05
)
raw_plot
close_vault(vault)
```

The fixture includes a small DIA-NN report source. A production vault needs that report for raw quantities or a `max_q_value` filter. The optional `qc` layer contains published cohort QC metrics. Inspect available metric names before plotting; they depend on the QC pipeline output.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
metrics <- tbl_qc_metrics(vault = vault)
available_metrics <- dplyr::collect(
    dplyr::distinct(metrics, metric_name)
)

metric_plot <- plot_qc_metric(
    vault = vault,
    metric_name = available_metrics$metric_name[[1L]],
    style = "ggplot2"
)

charge_plot <- plot_qc_charge_psm_counts(
    vault = vault,
    charges = 1:4,
    style = "BPG"
)

close_vault(vault)
```

`plot_qc_boxplot()` displays percentile summaries where the QC output supplies p05, p25, p50, p75, and p95 metrics. The `plot_qc_metric()`, `plot_qc_boxplot()`, and `plot_qc_charge_psm_counts()` functions accept source and fraction filters; see their R help pages. BPG plots return lattice objects, while the distribution plots return ggplot objects.
